questions.q: Given $x=4$. Column A: $(x+2)^2$. Column B: $x^2+4x+4$. Compare the two columns.
questions.target: Algebraic comparisons at a fixed value
questions.answer: $(x+2)^2$ expands to $x^2+4x+4$ for every value of $x$, so the columns are always equal. $A=B$.
questions.explanation: $(x+2)^2$ expands to $x^2+4x+4$ for every value of $x$, so the columns are always equal. $A=B$.

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Given $n=-2$. Column A: $n^2$. Column B: $n^3$. Compare the two columns.
questions.target: Algebraic comparisons at a fixed value

questions.q: Given $x=3$. Column A: $5x-2$. Column B: $2(x+5)$. Compare the two columns.
questions.target: Algebraic comparisons at a fixed value

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $x$. Column B: $x^2$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x=2$: $B>A$. If $x=\frac{1}{2}$: $A>B$. If $x=1$: $A=B$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.
questions.explanation: If $x=2$: $B>A$. If $x=\frac{1}{2}$: $A>B$. If $x=1$: $A=B$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $x+5$. Column B: $2x$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x=5$: $A=B$. If $x=0$: $A>B$. If $x=10$: $B>A$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.
questions.explanation: If $x=5$: $A=B$. If $x=0$: $A>B$. If $x=10$: $B>A$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $|x|$. Column B: $x$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $x\geq0$: $A=B$. If $x<0$ (e.g. $x=-3$): $A=3$, $B=-3$, so $A>B$. Since the relationship is not the same in every case, it cannot be determined.
questions.explanation: If $x\geq0$: $A=B$. If $x<0$ (e.g. $x=-3$): $A=3$, $B=-3$, so $A>B$. Since the relationship is not the same in every case, it cannot be determined.

questions.q: Given only that $n$ is an integer: Column A: $n^2$. Column B: $4$. Compare the two columns.
questions.answer: If $n=1$: $A=1<4$. If $n=3$: $A=9>4$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.
questions.explanation: If $n=1$: $A=1<4$. If $n=3$: $A=9>4$. The relationship changes, so it cannot be determined.

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $x^2$. Column B: $0$. Compare the two columns.
choices: The relationship cannot be determined from the given information
questions.answer: $x^2$ is always $\geq0$, but could equal $0$ (at $x=0$) or exceed it — not always the same relationship.
questions.explanation: $x^2$ is always $\geq0$, but could equal $0$ (at $x=0$) or exceed it — not always the same relationship.

questions.q: For any integer $n$: Column A: $n$. Column B: $-n$. Compare the two columns.
choices: The relationship cannot be determined from the given information
questions.answer: If $n>0$, A is greater; if $n<0$, B is greater; if $n=0$, they are equal — it varies.
questions.explanation: If $n>0$, A is greater; if $n<0$, B is greater; if $n=0$, they are equal — it varies.

questions.q: For any real number $x$ with $x\neq0$: Column A: $x^2$. Column B: $0$. Compare the two columns.
choices: The relationship cannot be determined from the given information
questions.answer: Since $x\neq0$, $x^2$ is always strictly positive, so Column A is always greater.
questions.explanation: Since $x\neq0$, $x^2$ is always strictly positive, so Column A is always greater.

choices: The relationship cannot be determined from the given information
questions.answer: At $m=1$ they are equal; for $m>1$, Column B is greater — it varies.
questions.explanation: At $m=1$ they are equal; for $m>1$, Column B is greater — it varies.

questions.q: For any real number $x$: Column A: $-x$. Column B: $x-1$. Compare the two columns.
choices: The relationship cannot be determined from the given information
questions.answer: $-x-(x-1)=1-2x$, whose sign depends on $x$ — it varies.
questions.explanation: $-x-(x-1)=1-2x$, whose sign depends on $x$ — it varies.

questions.q: Column A: the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon. Column B: the sum of the interior angles of two triangles.
choices: The relationship cannot be determined from the given information
questions.answer: Hexagon $=720^{\circ}$; two triangles $=180+180=360^{\circ}$. Column A is greater.
questions.explanation: Hexagon $=720^{\circ}$; two triangles $=180+180=360^{\circ}$. Column A is greater.
